text:
Jason Calacanis Identifies AI’s Biggest Opportunity: Adoption Is Still Nascent At Work

“Gallup's been keeping a survey of who's using AI at work.

The people using it frequently versus daily, we're still talking about 10 and 20% here. It's nascent.

A lot of the top enterprises are not letting their employees use this in an unconstrained fashion, and they're certainly not letting them connect their email, their knowledge bases, their Notions, their Slacks.

Big corporations are not letting people actually use the power of AI because they're scared about cyber.

So once the cyber threat gets mitigated, this is gonna go from 10% of people being daily users to 60, 70, 80%.

There's so much growth left here when every single employee has an agent. I saw just last week Uber bought ChatGPT for every employee.

That's going to be the next shoe to drop, do you buy these things for every single employee?”

Dan Held says IPOs give shareholders liquidity and ways to hedge, and calls it disappointing that Kraken still hasn't gone public

text:
Binance lost about $6.3 billion in Thursday's hack. It is the largest crypto theft on record in dollar terms, roughly four times the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025.

The drain started at 4:05 PM ET on Oct 29. TRM Labs says most of it left Binance wallets in about 20 minutes, across 10 blockchains.

Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover users. $5 billion of that is already held in the exact tokens that were stolen, about 80% of the loss. It is buying the rest through the market and OTC desks.

About $3 billion has been frozen on-chain, almost all of it $USDT and $USDC. The attacker still holds 18,270 $BTC split across 19 wallets. Elliptic says none of it has reached an exchange or service yet.

TRM and Chainalysis attribute the theft with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit. No government has confirmed it. Trump on Friday: "We don't know. We're looking at that." The FBI and Secret Service are both involved.

TRM counts $12.8 billion stolen by North Korea since 2017. $7.4 billion of it came this year.

Binance is targeting a phased restart of withdrawals early Sunday. Proof of reserves results are due Monday.

en_summary: Scott Melker quotes Dan Held saying crypto exchange price gaps are not arbitrage but premium for counterparty risk, requiring funds on every exchange, citing historical Mt. Gox vs Bitstamp.
text:
"You're not arbitraging anything."

Dan Held says the price gap between crypto exchanges isn't arbitrage, but a premium traders are paid for taking on counterparty risk

"I was talking to some arbitrage traders in crypto, and I'm like, you're not arbitraging anything."

"What you are arbing is the exchange counterparty risk, because you're putting funds at risk, and there's a small premium or discount because of that risk."

"To do that trade, you have to have funds on every exchange at all times. Both the token that you're trying to arbitrage and dollars of some sort."

"We saw this with Mt. Gox and Bitstamp. Back in the day, coins on Mt. Gox traded higher than Bitstamp. The reason why is that Mt. Gox's fiat legs, the ability to wire money out, had withdrawal issues. The only way to get your money out was to buy Bitcoin."

"And what we learned is that there's no arbitrage at all there. It was counterparty risk."

With midterms coming up next week, it’s important to remember that as hard as it may be, history shows that it’s not advisable to let politics impact your investment decisions.  We could provide countless examples where one side of the political aisle thought the stock market was doomed because the other side was set to take power, but the graphic below is an excellent case in point as well.

As shown, over the last nine sessions of Congress since the Financial Crisis, we’ve seen five of the eight possible combinations of party control in Washington, from one-party rule by both Democrats and Republicans twice each, to several forms of divided government.  While power in DC has changed hands again and again, there has been one constant: the S&P 500 has risen during every one of the last nine sessions.

(Past performance is no guarantee of future results!)
